assessments.reasoning: In spdx/license-list-data, annotated tag object 76c9a79bb7d2bf851143b76b3935a4d7cbaa644b names v3.29.0 and targets object type commit, SHA 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48. This is the revision in the ODbL detail URL.

Seven contiguous ranges cover all 114312 bytes of json/details/ODbL-1.0.json. Part 1 gives isDeprecatedLicenseId=false. Part 4 gives licenseId ODbL-1.0, name “Open Data Commons Open Database License v1.0” and both routes in crossRef and seeAlso.

As context, the pinned ODC HTML independently identifies the publisher-side v1.0 referent at the cited HTTPS URL. Its heading and §§3.1 and 4.4 distinguish it from ODC-By and PDDL. SPDX controls the identifier assignment.

challenge.method: Compared the tag object's target type and SHA with the detail locator. Checked case-sensitive identifier, title, deprecation, both publisher references and their match fields. Compared distinctive clauses against the other ODC editions and checked a concrete internal cross-reference.
challenge.results: The detail cites https://opendatacommons.org/licenses/odbl/1-0/ and http://www.opendatacommons.org/licenses/odbl/1.0/. Both crossRef match fields read “false”. The first URL is the inspected publisher edition, and §4.4 identifies the same share-alike instrument. In §4.7(b), SPDX licenseText reads “Section 4.74 a.” where the publisher reads “Section 4.7 a.” That discrepancy defeats a verbatim-text inference while leaving the documentary match intact.

limitations: The tag is unsigned. The repository API establishes the recorded target. The detail and tag share the SPDX Data authority chain.
The finding covers documentary correspondence. XML build lineage, complete textual or legal equivalence, rights in a particular database, and current behavior of the legacy URL fall outside it.
reasoning: The SPDX Data v3.29.0 tag targets the commit containing the ODbL-1.0 detail. That detail names the publisher edition and cites the exact inspected ODC HTTPS route. The publisher heading, database grant and share-alike clause confirm the referent. This meets SCES §7's requirement to pin the owning index and release and protocol stage 7's requirement to reopen the evidence and challenge the correspondence.
